rationale: Three blocking major findings across both repos: (1) The GIN index on assistants.toolkits added by the Alembic migration will not accelerate the jsonb_array_elements EXISTS query used by compose_credential_type_filter — PostgreSQL GIN indexes on JSONB support containment operators only, not set-returning function scans, so the migration adds write amplification with no read benefit; (2) filter_value=[None] (JSON [null]) bypasses all guards in compose_credential_type_filter and generates an IS NULL condition via SQLAlchemy's == None translation, returning incorrect results silently as HTTP 200; (3) Two frontend integration tests explicitly mandated by the spec are not implemented. One deferred item: enum validation at the router boundary (spec marks as 'should', non-blocking for MVP).

findings.problem: GIN index on assistants.toolkits will not accelerate the jsonb_array_elements EXISTS query used by compose_credential_type_filter
findings.impact: PostgreSQL GIN indexes on JSONB columns accelerate @>, ?, ?|, ?& operators only — not set-returning function scans (jsonb_array_elements is SRF). Every integration_type-filtered query performs a full sequential scan; the migration adds write amplification on every assistants INSERT/UPDATE with zero read benefit. The spec's performance intent (following the ix_assistants_categories precedent) is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the GIN index migration (correct for the current query pattern), or redesign the filter to use @> containment which GIN does accelerate — but note the spec explicitly chose EXISTS to avoid @> due to test-suite limitations with mocked sessions.

findings.problem: filter_value=[None] passes all guards and generates an IS NULL condition returning incorrect results silently
findings.impact: A client sending filters={"integration_type":[null]} results in values=[None] which is truthy and non-empty — both guard checks pass. SQLAlchemy translates .astext == None to '... IS NULL', returning assistants whose toolkit settings lack a credential_type key. Callers receive HTTP 200 with a misleading result set. The filter JSON is parsed with raw json.loads with no schema validation on element types.
findings.recommendation: Filter out None and empty-string entries after coercion: values = [v for v in (filter_value if isinstance(filter_value, list) else [filter_value]) if v is not None and v != '']

findings.problem: Two integration tests explicitly mandated by the spec are not implemented
findings.impact: End-to-end wiring of the integration_type filter to the API call layer is unverified by automated tests. Regressions in filter serialization, debounce timing, cleanObject stripping, or request construction will not be caught by CI.
findings.recommendation: Implement the two spec-required integration tests: (1) selecting a single integration_type value fires the correct API request with integration_type in the filters payload; (2) combining integration_type with a search term fires the correctly combined request.
